21 A signal generator, amplifier and loudspeaker are used to produce different sound waves in the
air of a room. The relationships between the properties of these waves are investigated.
Which relationship is not correct?
A
Amplitude is proportional to wavelength.
B
Frequency is inversely proportional to wavelength.
C
Intensity is proportional to amplitude squared at a given frequency.
D
Period is equal to the reciprocal of frequency.

hints: Notice the signal generator changes frequency while the amplifier changes loudness, so think about which control sets amplitude and which sets wavelength in the same room air.
Connect the sound speed in air to frequency and wavelength with $v = f\lambda$, with $v$ fixed, to test how $f$ varies with $\lambda$.
Recall the two standard wave rules being tested: $T = 1/f$ and, at fixed frequency, intensity $I$ proportional to (amplitude)$^2$, then look for the statement that links two independent controls.
walkthrough: Identify the setup: signal generator sets frequency $f$, amplifier sets amplitude $A$, and sound speed $v$ is fixed in the air of the same room.
Use $v = f\lambda$ with constant $v$ to give $f = v/\lambda$ and $\lambda = v/f$, so frequency is inversely proportional to wavelength.
Use the definitions $T = 1/f$, so period is the reciprocal of frequency.
Use the energy rule for waves: at a given frequency, intensity $I$ is proportional to amplitude squared, $I \propto A^2$.
Amplitude and wavelength are controlled independently, so amplitude is not proportional to wavelength and that statement is false. This is option A.

A.explanation: Amplitude set by the amplifier volume is independent of wavelength set by the signal generator frequency, so there is no proportional link.

B.explanation: For sound in the same room air, speed $v$ is constant and $v = f\lambda$, so $f = v/\lambda$ is inversely proportional to $\lambda$.

C.explanation: At a given frequency, wave intensity $I$ is proportional to amplitude squared, $I \propto A^2$.

D.explanation: By definition period and frequency are reciprocals, $T = 1/f$.
